items.title: FastGPT safe axios SSRF guard still allows DNS rebinding TOCTOU on protected outbound requests
items.summary: FastGPT is an open-source LLM platform for building AI applications on a knowledge base. Prior to 4.15.2, the safe Axios request interceptor in packages/service/common/api/axios.ts validates a hostname with isInternalAddress() before a later HTTP connection performs an independent DNS lookup, creating a DNS rebinding window, allowing an attacker-controlled hostname to resolve publicly during the check and to a loopback, private, link-local, or metadata address during connection. An authenticated attacker who can supply a URL to a safe-Axios-backed HTTP tool, workflow HTTP node, external file fetch, or other server-side integration can use this time-of-check/time-of-use gap to reach services that direct private-address inputs would block. The same independent re-resolution occurs after manual redirect hops because each redirect target is checked before a separate connection lookup. This issue is fixed in version 4.15.2.

items.title: MISP Collections: Missing Authorization Check for Sharing Group on PUT Request in collections/add
items.summary:
In MISP, the CollectionsController add() method enforced the sharing-group usability authorization check and element capture only when the HTTP request method was POST. However, the underlying CRUDComponent::add() method persists data on both POST and PUT requests. As a result, an authenticated user could issue a PUT request to the collections/add endpoint, bypassing the sharing-group authorization check entirely. This allowed the creation of a collection with distribution=4 (shared with a specific sharing group) targeting a sharing group that the user was not authorized to use. The bypassed check would normally verify that the current user has access to the specified sharing group before allowing the collection to be associated with it.

The security impact is that an authenticated user can place collection data into a sharing group context they do not have legitimate access to, potentially exposing that data to all members of the unauthorized sharing group and violating the intended access-control boundaries of the MISP instance.

The vulnerability requires an authenticated session and knowledge of a valid sharing group identifier; no user interaction or special tooling is needed beyond sending a PUT request instead of a POST request to the same endpoint.

items.title: Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile代码注入漏洞

llm_summary.summary_zh: 该条目来自知道创宇 / Seebug 漏洞库，标题为「Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile 代码注入漏洞」。Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile（EPMM，前身为 MobileIron Core）是企业级移动设备管理（MDM）平台，用于统一纳管 iOS / Android 等移动终端，负责设备注册与入网、合规策略下发、配置与证书分发、应用推送以及远程锁定与擦除等管理动作，通常部署在企业内网核心位置，部分场景下管理控制台或设备注册接口需要暴露到互联网以便终端随时接入。本次条目将其归类为代码注入类漏洞，从漏洞类别的通用语义看，代码注入通常意味着外部不可信输入在未经充分校验或转义的情况下进入了可执行上下文（例如脚本引擎、模板渲染、表达式解析或命令解析环节），当攻击者能够触达相关接口并构造特定输入时，可能导致服务进程执行非预期代码、被用于读取或篡改服务端数据，进而访问其托管的设备清单、策略配置与凭据材料。但由于该条目的正文摘要为空，未提供 CVE 编号、受影响产品版本区间、漏洞所在组件与入口点、触发所需权限（是否需认证）、攻击复杂度以及厂商是否已发布修复版本等关键信息，因此无法核实漏洞的真实性、可利用性与实际影响范围。条目给出的严重性为 unknown，且无任何参考链接，不能据此判断风险等级或是否已被在野利用。对防守方而言，当前可行动的结论是：将 EPMM 纳入重点资产清单，持续跟踪 Ivanti 官方安全公告与 Seebug 条目后续更新，待官方确认受影响版本与补丁后再评估修复优先级。

items.title: Hatchet DurableTask WorkerStatus gRPC resolves caller-supplied durable-task UUIDs via ListSatisfiedEntries with no tenant_id filter
items.summary:
# Cross-tenant disclosure risk on `DurableTask` bidi RPC

This is a low-severity, low-risk cross-tenant data exposure vuln caused by blindly accepting a durable task id, in addition to a list of node and branch ids that identify records in that task's event log, and returning them to the caller via the `handleWorkerStatus` polling path.

# Impact

This advisory requires an attacker to successfully guess a durable task's external uuid belonging to another tenant. External ids are generated uuid v4s (`uuid.New()` in Go), so exploitation requires prior knowledge of a target task UUID through an out-of-band channel. Thus, while the following environments are impacted, there is an extremely low probability it would be exploited.

### Who is impacted. Any Hatchet deployment that hosts more than one tenant on the same instance:

* Hatchet Cloud (multi-tenant SaaS)
* Self-hosted Hatchet with multiple internal teams / business units sharing one instance
* Any deployment where a single tenant's API token can be obtained by an attacker

Single-tenant self-hosted deployments are unaffected in practice (the "victim" and "attacker" tenants would be the same).

items.title: Hatchet: Cross-tenant durable callback payload disclosure in Hatchet V1 Dispatcher
items.summary:
## Summary

The V1 `DurableTask` stream handler registers worker-supplied durable task external IDs in an in-memory callback routing map before verifying that the authenticated tenant owns the task. If the tenant-scoped ownership check fails, the handler logs the error and continues, but the map entry persists until the stream closes.

Durable callback delivery resolves the destination stream by `task_external_id` only, without checking tenant identity. As a result, a tenant A worker that knows a tenant B durable task external UUID can hold its stream open and receive tenant B's durable callback result payload when the callback is delivered on the same dispatcher process.

## Impact

This advisory requires an attacker to successfully guess a durable task external UUID belonging to another tenant. Durable task external IDs are generated with `uuid.New()` (UUIDv4) and are not enumerable across tenants, so exploitation requires prior knowledge of a target task UUID through an out-of-band channel. Thus, while the following environments are impacted, there is an extremely low probability it would be exploited. 

**Who is impacted.** Any Hatchet deployment that hosts more than one tenant on the same instance:
- Hatchet Cloud (multi-tenant SaaS) 
- Self-hosted Hatchet with multiple internal teams / business units sharing one instance
- Any deployment where a single tenant's API token can be obtained by an attacker

Single-tenant self-hosted deployments are unaffected in practice (the "victim" and "attacker" tenants would be the same).

items.title: Cloudreve: Privilege Scope Bypass: State-Mutating Admin Operations Accessible via Read-Only OAuth Scope
items.summary:
### Summary
There is a privilege scope bypass in Cloudreve's admin API where two endpoints that mutate server state are missing the write-scope enforcement that their neighboring endpoints correctly apply. Specifically, the WOPI configuration fetch endpoint and the SMTP test/mail endpoint can both be triggered by an OAuth token that only has Admin.Read authorization — no Admin.Write needed. This breaks the intended OAuth scope boundary in a way that's subtle enough to have slipped through but meaningful enough to matter in a real deployment.

### Details
The root cause is an inconsistency in how the admin tool routes are wired up in `routers/router.go`. The admin route group sets a baseline of `ScopeAdminRead` for everything underneath it (around line 868), and most write-capable endpoints inside the `tool` sub-group correctly layer on an additional `RequiredScopes(types.ScopeAdminWrite)` check on top of that. For example, the thumbnail executable setter (line 929) and the entity URL cache deletion (line 937) both do this properly.

The two endpoints that don't follow this pattern are `tool.GET('wopi')` (line 925) and `tool.POST('mail')` (line 933). Despite `POST /mail` clearly triggering an outbound email and `GET /wopi` fetching or probing WOPI service connectivity, neither has the `ScopeAdminWrite` guard. What that means in practice is that any OAuth application granted only Admin.Read — a scope that should be limited to inspecting configuration, not changing anything — can silently invoke both of these operations. The developer looking at the route definitions would reasonably assume all the write-adjacent tool endpoints were protected, because the ones right above and below them are. It's the kind of gap that's easy to miss in a code review.

### PoC
```bash
# OAuth app with ONLY Admin.Read scope can send emails:
curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_READ_ONLY_TOKEN>' \
  'https://cloudreve.example.com/api/v4/admin/tool/mail' \
  -d '{"settings":{"smtpHost":"smtp.gmail.com","smtpPort":"587",...},"to":"victim@example.com"}'
# Expected: 403 Forbidden (if Admin.Write was required)
# Actual: 200 OK, email is sent
```

### Impact
An OAuth application or API key scoped to Admin.Read can send arbitrary emails through the server's configured SMTP account and probe internal WOPI service endpoints — both actions that should require elevated write authorization. In multi-party deployments where Admin.Read tokens are issued more liberally (e.g., to monitoring integrations or third-party plugins), a compromised or malicious token holder gains capabilities well beyond what the scope contract implies. Scope separation in OAuth 2.0 is a security boundary, not just a convention, and its violation here could factor into broader attack chains.

### Fix
Add `middleware.RequiredScopes(types.ScopeAdminWrite)` as the first handler argument to both the `tool.GET('wopi')` and `tool.POST('mail')` route definitions in `routers/router.go`. This brings them in line with `tool.POST('thumbExecutable')` at line 929 and `tool.DELETE('entityUrlCache')` at line 937, which already follow the correct pattern. No logic changes are needed — it's purely an additive middleware insertion.

**If possible, please apply for a CVE number when publishing. I would greatly appreciate it.**

items.title: lightrag-hku: SSRF via IPv6-transition address bypass (NAT64, IPv4-compatible, 6to4) of the native-markdown image-download guard
items.summary:
## Summary

LightRAG's native markdown parser downloads external images referenced by an uploaded markdown or textpack document. The only SSRF guard, `_validated_addresses()` in `lightrag/parser/markdown/parser.py`, resolves the image host and rejects it when the resolved IP is not `is_global`. That check is evaluated on the raw resolved address and never decodes IPv6 transition wrappers that embed an internal IPv4. Python's `ipaddress` classifies a NAT64 (`64:ff9b::/96` and the RFC 8215 `64:ff9b:1::/48` prefix), IPv4-compatible (`::a.b.c.d`), or 6to4 (`2002::/16`) literal that wraps an internal IPv4 as globally routable, so the guard passes it. On a host with NAT64/DNS64 routing the request is then delivered to the embedded internal target (loopback, RFC1918, or a cloud metadata endpoint), and the fetched body is ingested. The plain and IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:`) forms of the same internal address are correctly blocked, so this is an encoding that defeats the existing filter.

## Affected component and versions

- Package: `lightrag-hku` (LightRAG), the native markdown image-download path.
- Component: `lightrag/parser/markdown/parser.py`, guard `_validated_addresses()` (the `if not (ip.is_global or ...)` check), reached from `_download()` -> `_build_guarded_opener().open(req)`.
- Enabled by default: `download_enabled = _env_bool("NATIVE_MD_IMAGE_DOWNLOAD_ENABLED", True)`.
- Affected: LightRAG `<= 1.5.4` (latest release at time of report, commit `9a45b64`).
- Precondition: the caller can upload a document (API key via `Depends(combined_auth)`); the host has NAT64/DNS64 routing for the encoded address to reach the internal endpoint.

## Vulnerable code vs the guarded sibling

Evaluated on the exact resolved addresses (CPython `ipaddress`):

| Form | address | is_global | guard verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain internal 127.0.0.1 | `127.0.0.1` | False | BLOCK (correct) |
| IPv4-mapped | `::ffff:7f00:1` | False | BLOCK (correct) |
| NAT64 64:ff9b::/96 | `64:ff9b::7f00:1` | True | PASS (bypass) |
| NAT64 RFC8215 64:ff9b:1::/48 | `64:ff9b:1::7f00:1` | True | PASS (bypass) |
| IPv4-compatible ::a.b.c.d | `::7f00:1` | True | PASS (bypass) |
| 6to4 2002::/16 | `2002:7f00:1::` | True | PASS (bypass) |

items.title: lightrag-hku: No Rate Limiting on /login Endpoint Allows Brute-Force Attacks
items.summary:
### Summary
The POST /login endpoint has no rate limiting, account lockout, or delay on failed attempts. An attacker can submit unlimited password guesses at full network speed.

### Details

```python
# lightrag/api/lightrag_server.py:2161
@app.post("/login")
async def login(form_data: OAuth2PasswordRequestForm = Depends()):
    if not auth_handler.verify_password(username, form_data.password):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Incorrect credentials")
    # No: rate limit / lockout / backoff / CAPTCHA / attempt counter
```

A search for slowapi, rate_limit, lockout, or throttle in lightrag/api/ returns zero results.

### PoC

```bash
# Brute-force /login with a wordlist, no throttling
while IFS= read -r pass; do
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
    -X POST http://<TARGET>:9621/login \
    -d "username=admin&password=${pass}")
  [ "$code" = "200" ] && echo "[FOUND] $pass" && break
done < /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
```

### Impact
Improper restriction of authentication attempts. Any network-reachable attacker can brute-force user passwords without restriction. Once credentials are recovered, the attacker gains full authenticated access to all documents, knowledge graph, and administrative operations.

items.title: KubeEdge: Unbounded allocation in viaduct packer enables authenticated remote DoS against CloudHub
items.summary:
## Summary

KubeEdge CloudHub uses the viaduct packer to decode messages received from connected peers. The packer reads a 32-bit payload length from the message header and previously allocated a buffer of that size without enforcing an upper bound.

An authenticated peer that can establish a viaduct connection to CloudHub can send a crafted message header containing an excessively large payload length. This may cause CloudHub to allocate a large amount of memory and can result in memory exhaustion, process termination, or denial of service.

## Impact

A successfully authenticated malicious or compromised edge node may repeatedly send crafted viaduct message headers to increase CloudHub memory consumption.

Depending on available memory and deployment limits, exploitation may cause:

* Increased CloudHub memory usage
* Out-of-memory termination
* CloudHub restart loops
* Temporary disruption of cloud-edge communication

Authentication to the viaduct endpoint is required. This issue does not provide unauthenticated access or direct code execution.

## Root cause

The viaduct packer trusted the payload length encoded in the message header and allocated the payload buffer before validating whether the declared length was within an acceptable range.

## Fix

The fix introduces a maximum viaduct payload size of 32 MiB.

The updated implementation:

* Rejects oversized payload lengths in the reader before memory allocation
* Enforces the same maximum size in the writer
* Adds regression tests covering oversized and valid payloads

Fixes have been prepared for the following patch releases:

* KubeEdge v1.23.1
* KubeEdge v1.22.2
* KubeEdge v1.21.2

These versions should not be listed as released until the coordinated release process is complete.

## Workarounds

Before patched versions are available, operators should:

* Restrict access to the CloudHub endpoint to trusted edge nodes and networks
* Protect and rotate edge-node credentials
* Revoke credentials belonging to decommissioned or potentially compromised nodes
* Apply memory limits and restart policies to the CloudHub workload
* Monitor CloudHub memory consumption and unexpected connection activity

## Affected component

* `pkg/viaduct/pkg/packer`
* CloudHub viaduct message-processing path

## Credits

KubeEdge thanks Sang-Hoon Choi ([KoreaSecurity](https://github.com/KoreaSecurity), Sejong University)
for responsibly reporting this issue and for coordinating with the KubeEdge
maintainers through the security disclosure process.

items.title: 从一个辅助 API 看资源边界：CVE-2026-71486（vLLM）

llm_summary.summary_zh: 先知社区发布一篇针对 vLLM（主流大语言模型推理与在线服务框架）的技术分析文章，标题为《从一个辅助 API 看资源边界：CVE-2026-71486（vLLM）》，讨论编号为 CVE-2026-71486 的安全问题。文章以 vLLM 对外提供的『辅助 API』（即非核心推理主链路之外的次要/管理类接口，如健康检查、指标、模型与分词等辅助端点）为切入点，考察其在资源边界（resource boundary）上的处理方式，暗示该问题的核心可能与辅助接口未正确实施资源限制或权限/隔离边界有关——例如在未鉴权或低权限可达的情况下触发超出预期的 CPU/GPU/显存/请求队列消耗，或越过预期的资源与租户隔离。vLLM 通常以 OpenAI 兼容的 HTTP 服务形式部署在自建 GPU 集群或 Kubernetes 环境中，常被用作企业内多租户推理网关，因此这类次要接口一旦暴露在不可信网络，就可能成为长期被忽视的攻击面。需要强调的是，当前可获取的信息仅有标题与来源元数据，正文内容未提供：漏洞的具体成因、攻击前置条件、受影响版本区间、是否已有修复版本、以及该 CVE 在真实攻击链中的角色（资源耗尽型拒绝服务、权限绕过还是信息暴露）均无法确认。本条目按『漏洞技术研究』类情报处理，尚无任何在野利用、武器化或攻击者归因的证据。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: vLLM 是大量企业自建大模型推理服务的核心组件，常直接对内网或公网提供 OpenAI 兼容接口；若辅助 API 的资源边界存在缺陷，可能造成资源耗尽型拒绝服务或租户/资源隔离被绕过，波及多租户 GPU 集群。虽暂无在野利用证据，但『被忽视的次要接口』历来是真实攻击入口，值得优先排查与加固。

llm_summary.recommended_action_zh: 1) 持续跟踪 vLLM 官方安全公告与该 CVE 的修复版本，确认自身部署版本后及时升级；2) 收敛攻击面：将辅助/管理类端点（指标、健康检查、模型管理等）限定在内网、管理网或经鉴权代理后方，避免直接暴露到公网；3) 在反向代理或 API 网关层对全部路径（含辅助接口）统一实施鉴权、限流、请求体大小与超时限制；4) 加强资源侧监控与告警：GPU 显存、请求队列长度、连接数、单 IP 并发与异常长/超大请求，发现异常立即封禁并留存证据；5) 多租户环境配置资源配额与隔离策略，评估次要接口是否可绕过配额；6) 日志排查与威胁狩猎：回溯历史访问日志中辅助端点的高频或异常调用模式，确认是否已被探测或滥用；7) 若短期内无法升级，优先通过网关策略与网络分段做补偿性控制。

items.title: D-Link warns of max severity zero-day bug in DIR-822A routers
items.summary: D-Link warned customers of a maximum-severity vulnerability (CVE-2026-86296) with public proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit code and no patch, affecting legacy DIR-822A dual-band Wi-Fi routers. [...]

llm_summary.summary_zh: D-Link 发布安全公告，警告其已停止支持的旧款 DIR-822A 双频 Wi-Fi 路由器存在一个最高严重等级（Max Severity）的零日漏洞，编号 CVE-2026-86296。该漏洞目前没有官方补丁，且公开的漏洞验证代码（PoC）已在互联网上流传，攻击门槛被显著降低，任何能够接触到受影响设备管理接口的一方都可能尝试利用。原文摘要未披露漏洞的具体技术类型（如命令注入、缓冲区溢出或认证绕过）与触发条件，因此该漏洞在潜在攻击链中的确切角色尚不明确——既可能是初始访问入口，也可能被用于权限提升或持久化。受影响范围集中在仍在使用 DIR-822A 的家庭用户、小型办公网络，以及把此类消费级路由器作为边缘设备部署的环境；由于该型号已处于生命周期终止（EOL）状态，预计不会获得固件修复，用户只能通过更换设备或收紧网络暴露面来缓解风险。BleepingComputer 的报道属于媒体对厂商公告的转述，尚无独立研究机构公开完整的根因分析或威胁狩猎数据，也没有证据显示该漏洞已被勒索软件团伙或其他攻击者实际利用。建议安全团队立即清点资产中是否存在 DIR-822A 及同系列 EOL 路由器，重点关注面向 WAN 侧暴露的管理端口、远程管理与 UPnP 等功能，将其隔离到独立网段并限制入站访问，同时评估尽快退役替换。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 消费级/IoT 边缘设备零日且无补丁，公开 PoC 进一步降低利用门槛；EOL 设备无法靠升级修复，只能依赖资产替换与网络隔离。若被攻陷可成为进入内网的跳板，需优先清点处置。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 影响仍在使用 DIR-822A 等已终止支持路由器的家庭与小型办公网络。设备若在互联网侧暴露管理接口，可能被完全控制并用作内网跳板。官方无补丁，实际影响面取决于存量设备规模与暴露情况。
llm_summary.recommended_action_zh: 1) 资产清点：排查全网是否存在 DIR-822A 及同系列 EOL 路由器，建立存量清单与责任人。2) 收敛暴露面：关闭 WAN 侧远程管理与 UPnP，禁止从互联网直接访问设备管理界面，仅允许受控内网或管理网段访问。3) 网络隔离：将此类设备划入独立 VLAN/访客网段，限制其向内网横向访问，仅放行必要出站流量。4) 替代退役：推动更换为仍在支持周期内、有固件更新渠道的型号，替换前优先处理公网暴露实例。5) 监控与检测：对路由器管理页面的异常登录、配置变更、固件/脚本写入及可疑出站连接建立日志告警规则；在边界与 DNS 层监测异常外联。6) 威胁狩猎：针对已知存在公网暴露 EOL 设备的网段排查异常代理、隧道与会话，结合流量基线识别被控迹象。7) 持续跟踪厂商公告与 CVE-2026-86296 后续更新，若发布缓解措施或替代型号建议及时落地。

llm_summary.summary_zh: 本文为 CrowdStrike 于 2026-09-23 发布的官方产品公告，标题为《CrowdStrike 为 AI Agent 推出 Continuous Identity（持续身份）》。从标题与厂商定位来看，该能力面向的是企业环境中快速增长的「非人类身份」（Non-Human Identity, NHI）——即 AI 代理、自动化工作流、服务账号、API 令牌等在无人实时干预下自主调用系统和数据的实体。公告的核心主张是对 AI Agent 的身份进行持续性的识别、验证与行为治理，而不是仅在创建或登录时做一次性认证，目标是把身份安全从静态的账号目录管理，推进到对代理身份的运行时姿态（posture）与行为监控。结合 CrowdStrike 以 Falcon 平台为主的 EDR/XDR 产品线，可以合理推断该能力会与终端遥测、云工作负载与身份日志打通，用于发现权限过宽、长期有效凭据、异常代理调用链等风险场景。需要特别说明：本次输入的正文摘要为空，仅有标题、来源链接与标签，因此以上技术细节属于基于厂商产品定位的合理推断，而非原文确认的具体功能清单，实际能力范围（是否包含令牌生命周期管理、代理间信任关系图谱、异常行为检测规则等）需以原文为准。此外，输入的标签中包含 apt、edr、crowdstrike，并列出可能的恶意软件家族 Conti，但公告本身是产品发布类内容，未提供任何攻击活动、受害者、TTP 或 IOC 证据，Conti 与本文主题（AI 代理身份治理）无可见关联，应视为自动标注产生的噪声，不宜据此调整检测优先级。整体而言，这是一条产品/能力动态，而非威胁情报事件。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: AI 代理与服务账号等非人类身份正成为企业新的攻击面：长期有效凭据、过宽权限、缺乏行为基线，一旦被滥用极难察觉。厂商把身份治理延伸到 AI 代理，意味着防御方需将 NHI 纳入资产清点、权限收敛与运行时监控，否则 IAM 与 EDR 会出现监控盲区。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 影响面在于企业身份与云安全架构：若 AI 代理身份未被纳入治理与监控，可能出现凭据泄露、权限滥用、数据越权访问等风险，且传统以人为中心的检测手段难以覆盖。本文为厂商能力公告，无具体受害对象或攻击事件，暂无直接事件影响。
llm_summary.recommended_action_zh: 1) 资产盘点：梳理企业中 AI 代理、服务账号、API 令牌、CI/CD 机器人账号等非人类身份清单，明确责任人。2) 权限收敛：按最小权限原则复核其云资源、数据和 SaaS 访问范围，禁用长期不用的凭据。3) 凭据治理：优先采用短期令牌与自动轮换，减少静态密钥硬编码。4) 检测与日志：确保代理调用相关的云审计日志、身份提供方日志、API 网关日志集中留存，并对异常时段、异常地域、异常高频调用设置告警。5) 行为基线：为关键代理建立正常调用模式基线，对权限提升、横向访问、批量数据读取等偏离行为做威胁狩猎。6) 与现有 EDR/XDR、ITDR 能力对接，把代理身份事件纳入统一告警与响应流程。

items.title: SelfOp: An Optimization Algorithm for Self-Improving Security Agents
items.summary: LLM agents are increasingly used for security tasks: vulnerability discovery, exploit reproduction, and patch generation. Improving them at the model level demands expert demonstrations or computable rewards, which security tasks rarely offer: traces are costly, failures hard to diagnose, rewards sparse, and non-computable. Efforts thus shift to the harness and context, but manual tuning needs task-specific expertise and scales poorly, while automated methods rely on scarce ground truth, stronger optimizer models, or unguided propose-and-evaluate loops that reduce to costly trial and error. We introduce SelfOp, an algorithm that automatically improves a frozen security agent's task context (instructions, skills, and reference documents), without modifying its execution harness and model weights. SelfOp casts context optimization as chain-rule-inspired textual gradient descent: from a single instance's outcome, it propagates error signals backward through the evaluator, the agent's trajectory, and the context artifacts that shaped its behavior, yielding per-instance textual gradients. Gradients are accumulated across instances by clustering, ranking, and filtering, and committed only under cross-instance consensus. A convergence detector monitors the gradient signal itself and stops once the context has absorbed the generalizable information in the training data, without held-out validation data. We evaluate SelfOp on CyberGym, a benchmark of real-world vulnerability reproduction tasks. With fewer than 200 training examples, SelfOp yields a 17-point self-improvement for GPT-5.4-mini (with Codex), enough to surpass the frontier GPT-5.4 baseline by 6 points, and an 18.5-point self-improvement for GPT-5.4 itself. The optimized skills also transfer across models, highlighting that SelfOp-optimized skills learn generalizable task knowledge not model-specific patterns.

llm_summary.summary_zh: LLM 智能体正被用于漏洞发现、漏洞复现与补丁生成等安全任务，但在模型层面提升其能力通常依赖专家演示或可计算奖励，而安全任务恰恰很少具备这两点：执行轨迹昂贵、失败原因难以诊断、奖励稀疏且难以自动判定。因此研究重心转向执行框架（harness）与上下文（指令、技能、参考文档），但人工调优需要任务专家且难以扩展；自动化方法则依赖稀缺的标注真值、更强的优化器模型，或退化为盲目『提议—评估』的高成本试错。本文提出 SelfOp，一种在不修改模型权重、也不改动执行框架的前提下，自动优化冻结智能体任务上下文的算法。SelfOp 将上下文优化建模为受链式法则启发的文本梯度下降：从单条实例的执行结果出发，把误差信号经由评估器、智能体轨迹反向传播到塑造其行为的上下文制品，得到逐实例的文本梯度；再通过聚类、排序与过滤跨实例累积梯度，且仅在跨实例共识下才提交更新。算法还包含收敛检测器，直接监控梯度信号，在上下文已吸收训练数据中可泛化信息时停止，无需留出验证集。作者在 CyberGym 真实漏洞复现基准上评估：训练样本不足 200 条时，GPT-5.4-mini（配合 Codex）自我提升 17 分，超过前沿 GPT-5.4 基线 6 分；GPT-5.4 自身提升 18.5 分。优化后的技能还能跨模型迁移，说明其学到的是可泛化的任务知识而非模型特定模式。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 安全智能体的能力提升长期受限于专家标注与稀疏奖励。SelfOp 展示了无需改模型、仅用少量样本即可自动优化上下文与技能，并可跨模型迁移，为 SOC 自动化、漏洞复现与补丁生成智能体的持续调优提供了低成本可复用路径；同时也提示上下文与技能资产正成为新的供应链与投毒面。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 可迁移至漏洞复现、补丁生成、告警研判、取证分析等安全智能体工作流的自动化调优；对自建 LLM 安全 agent 的团队，可直接借鉴其『文本梯度+跨实例共识』范式来降低专家调参成本，但需警惕优化循环本身被投毒或过拟合基准。
detection_signals_zh: 智能体系统提示词、技能文件或参考文档出现异常频繁或未经审批的变更
短时间内对同一任务族产生大量失败-重试轨迹并伴随上下文自动改写
优化循环出现对基准数据集的非预期访问或验证集信息泄漏迹象
defense_advice_zh: 将 agent 的指令、技能与参考文档纳入版本控制与变更审计，提交前进行人工或自动化评审
在隔离环境中运行自动优化循环，限制其对生产工具与敏感数据的访问权限
对优化产出的技能包做来源与内容完整性校验，防止上下文投毒
保留独立基线评测集做回归，防止上下文过拟合训练任务导致泛化下降
llm_summary.recommended_action_zh: 研究跟进

items.title: LightRAG: No Rate Limiting on /login Endpoint Allows Brute-Force Attacks
items.summary: LightRAG provides simple and fast retrieval-augmented generation. Prior to 1.5.5, the POST /login endpoint in lightrag/api/lightrag_server.py does not impose a rate limit, account lockout, delay, or counter for failed authentication attempts. A network attacker can submit password guesses at full request speed until a valid account password is found. Successful credential recovery grants authenticated access to documents, the knowledge graph, and administrative operations. This issue is fixed in version 1.5.5.

items.title: 9Router: Login Brute-Force Lockout Bypass via Spoofable X-9r-Real-Ip Header
items.summary: 9Router is an AI router & token saver. Prior to 0.5.6, 9Router deployments that allow requests to reach Next.js without the sanitizing custom-server.js wrapper use the client-supplied X-9r-Real-Ip value as the bucket key in getClientIp, checkLock, and recordFail in src/lib/auth/loginLimiter.js for POST /api/auth/login. A remote unauthenticated attacker can rotate the header on every password guess so each request uses a new failed-attempt bucket and the five-attempt progressive lockout never returns HTTP 429. This permits unthrottled password guessing against the dashboard login and can lead to an administrative session if the password is recovered. This issue is fixed in version 0.5.6.

items.title: 9Router: Authentication Bypass in Public LLM API via Spoofable X-9r-Real-Ip Header
items.summary: 9Router is an AI router & token saver. Prior to 0.5.6, 9Router deployments that allow requests to reach Next.js without the sanitizing custom-server.js wrapper trust the client-supplied X-9r-Real-Ip header in src/dashboardGuard.js when isLocalRequest decides whether canAccessPublicLlmApi may skip API-key validation for /api/v1/* routes. A remote unauthenticated attacker can set X-9r-Real-Ip to 127.0.0.1 and be classified as a local client, including on the verified GET /api/v1/models route. This permits unauthorized use of the instance owner's configured LLM providers, consumption of paid credits, and enumeration of configured providers and models. This issue is fixed in version 0.5.6.

items.title: Spree: Broken Access Control in `PATCH /api/v3/store/carts/:id/associate` (IDOR)
items.summary: Spree is an open source e-commerce solution built with Ruby on Rails. From 5.4.0 until 5.4.4 and 5.5.4, PATCH /api/v3/store/carts/:id/associate in Spree::Api::V3::Store::CartsController#associate uses find_cart_for_association to locate a cart by prefixed_id but does not require a cart token or otherwise verify possession of the selected guest cart. An authenticated customer can derive reversible prefixed cart IDs, associate an eligible guest cart with the attacker's account, and receive billing and shipping address data from the cart. Exploitation requires a guest cart with address data on a store that does not require login for checkout, and reassignment can also disrupt the guest's in-progress cart. This issue is fixed in versions 5.4.4 and 5.5.4.

items.title: LightRAG: SSRF via IPv6-transition address bypass (NAT64, IPv4-compatible, 6to4) of the native-markdown image-download guard
items.summary: LightRAG provides simple and fast retrieval-augmented generation. Prior to 1.5.5, _validated_addresses in lightrag/parser/markdown/parser.py evaluates the literal resolved address with ipaddress.is_global without consistently classifying an IPv4 address embedded in an IPv6 transition wrapper. A caller who can upload a Markdown or textpack document can supply an external image URL using NAT64 64:ff9b::/96 or an IPv4-compatible form that embeds a loopback, private, or cloud-metadata IPv4 address. On a deployment with compatible NAT64 or DNS64 routing, _download and _build_guarded_opener accept the wrapper and fetch the internal resource, whose body is then ingested. Current interpreter behavior already blocks some RFC 8215 and 6to4 forms, but the fixed guard handles all documented wrappers without becoming more permissive than the standard library. This issue is fixed in version 1.5.5.

items.title: Cloudreve: Storage-quota TOCTOU race allows quota bypass and storage-based denial of service
items.summary: Cloudreve is a self-hosted file management and sharing system. Prior to 4.18.0, PrepareUpload in pkg/filemanager/fs/dbfs/upload.go checks a stale in-memory user storage value through validateUserCapacity and later applies an unconditional storage charge outside the same quota-enforcing transaction. An authenticated user with Files.Write permission can issue concurrent upload-session requests that read the same capacity snapshot, all pass the MaxStorage check, and reserve their declared sizes through CommitWithStorageDiff. The resulting reservations can exceed the account quota and can be materialized as chunked uploads that exhaust host storage and deny uploads to other users. The default local-storage policy and default User group are affected. This issue is fixed in version 4.18.0.

items.title: MISP Reflected Cross-Site Scripting in Event Export Confirmation Form via Unescaped JSON
items.summary:
MISP contains a reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the event REST search export confirmation form. The view template app/View/Events/ajax/eventRestSearchExportConfirmationForm.ctp renders a URL-supplied event ID list into a single-quoted JavaScript string literal using PHP's json_encode() without any hex-encoding flags. By default, json_encode() escapes double quotes and backslashes but does not escape single quotes. Because the JavaScript string is delimited by single quotes, an attacker can inject a single-quote character to terminate the string literal and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser session.

The vulnerability affects the Default and UiBeta themes, both of which render this view. The Overmind theme's own copy of the form already passed the value through an escaped data attribute and was not affected by this specific sink.

Preconditions: the victim must be an authenticated MISP user and must actively open or navigate to the attacker-crafted URL. The attacker does not require an account or any prior access to the MISP instance.

Security impact: successful exploitation allows execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the MISP web application, potentially leading to session hijacking, unauthorized actions performed on behalf of the victim, exfiltration of sensitive data visible in the session, or further client-side attacks. The vulnerable component's own confidentiality, integrity, and availability are not directly compromised; the impact is on the underlying user session.

items.title: MISP CSRF vulnerability in workflow moduleStatelessExecution allows cross-site execution of workflow modules
items.summary:
MISP's WorkflowsController exposed the moduleStatelessExecution action in the Security component's unlockedActions list. In CakePHP, listing an action in unlockedActions disables both the CSRF token check and the field hash validation for that action. Because moduleStatelessExecution executes a workflow module's exec() method with caller-supplied input and parameters, the absence of CSRF protection allowed an attacker to craft a cross-site form post (or equivalent cross-origin request) that, when submitted by an authenticated site administrator, would cause the administrator's browser to invoke the action on the MISP instance. 

The attacker could select any workflow module to execute, including action modules that write blocklist and warninglist entries, and supply arbitrary input and parameters of their choosing. This constitutes a cross-site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability with high integrity impact on the MISP instance's security-related data. 

The vulnerability was identified during an internal security review and was not externally reported. The fix is included in MISP v2.5.47.

items.title: Chartbrew: DNS Rebinding SSRF Bypass in Outbound Request Validation
items.summary: Chartbrew is an open-source web application that can connect directly to databases and APIs and use the data to create charts. Prior to 5.2.2, Chartbrew's server/modules/safeRequest.js calls validateOutboundUrl() to resolve and validate a target hostname, but request-promise performs a separate DNS resolution for the actual connection. An authenticated user who can create or test API connections and controls the target DNS name can return a public address during validation and a private address during the request, bypassing the protections implemented by server/modules/outboundTargetPolicy.js. This DNS rebinding condition can expose internal services, localhost resources, or cloud metadata endpoints. This issue is fixed in version 5.2.2.

items.title: lightrag-hku: Sensitive Information Exposure Through Raw Exception Messages in API Error Responses
items.summary:
### Summary

The LightRAG API server passes raw Python exception messages directly into HTTP
error responses across 30+ error handlers in every router. When combined with
the default unauthenticated configuration (see companion report on CWE-306), any
network-reachable client can trigger exceptions whose raw text discloses
internal infrastructure — server filesystem paths, database host/port/user, LLM
provider error details, and Python library internals. No global exception
handler sanitizes error messages before they reach the client.

### Details

Throughout the API route handlers, exceptions are caught and their string
representation is returned verbatim via `detail=str(e)` / `detail=str(exc)`
(and f-string variants such as `detail=f"...: {str(e)}"`). This occurs in every
router file. Location breakdown on the current `main` branch:

**HTTP 500 — raw exception passthrough (`except Exception as e`):**
- `document_routes.py` — 13
- `graph_routes.py` — 12 (mix of `detail=f"...{str(e)}"` and `detail=error_msg`)
- `query_routes.py` — 3
- `ollama_api.py` — 2
- `lightrag_server.py` — 1 (health endpoint)

**HTTP 422 — raw exception passthrough (`except ValueError as exc`):**
- `document_routes.py` — 2 (chunking-config validation)

**Total: ~33 raw-exception-to-HTTP-response locations.** The only pre-existing
custom exception handler in `lightrag_server.py` is specific to
`RequestValidationError` for `/query/data`; it does not cover the generic
`Exception` handlers in route code.

Example pattern (`document_routes.py`, upload handler):

```python
except Exception as e:
    logger.error(f"Error /documents/upload: {file.filename}: {str(e)}")
    raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e))
```

**Categories of sensitive information that can leak through these responses:**

1. **Server filesystem paths.** File-I/O errors from the default JSON storage
   backend expose the server's directory layout
   (e.g. `[Errno 13] Permission denied: '/app/data/rag_storage/default/kv_store_full_docs.json'`),
   aiding path-traversal or targeted attacks. *(Verified — see PoC Step 1.)*

2. **Database host / port / user / database name.** Connection errors from the
   PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, or Neo4j backends surface the target the driver
   was trying to reach — e.g. asyncpg raises
   `password authentication failed for user "lightrag"` (username) or a socket
   error naming the unreachable host and port.
   **Note on credentials:** the PostgreSQL backend uses `asyncpg`, which is
   built from keyword parameters and does **not** echo the password in its
   exception strings — so a raw asyncpg error leaks host/port/user/db, not the
   password. URI-configured backends behave differently: the MongoDB backend is
   built with `AsyncMongoClient(MONGO_URI, ...)`, and a malformed-URI /
   configuration error from pymongo can surface the connection string itself,
   which may embed credentials (`mongodb://user:password@host:port/`). The leak
   surface is therefore backend- and error-type-dependent.

3. **LLM provider error details.** Errors from OpenAI / Gemini / Bedrock and
   other providers may include model names, organization ids, or partial API
   error context that reveal the deployment.

4. **Python library internals.** Unexpected exceptions expose class names,
   library-internal messages, and stack fragments that fingerprint the server
   stack and version.

5. **Configuration details.** Errors during configuration/parsing may reveal
   storage backend types and other configuration values.

The risk is amplified by the default unauthenticated configuration (CWE-306,
companion report), which lets any network client trigger and read these errors
without credentials.

Tested on a clean checkout with the `[api]` extras installed and the server run
via `lightrag-server`.

items.title: KubeEdge: Command Injection in NodeUpgradeJob - RCE on edge nodes via v1alpha2 API
items.summary:
## Impact

The KubeEdge NodeUpgradeJob handler constructed the `keadm upgrade edge` command by concatenating the user-controlled `spec.version` and `spec.image` fields into a shell command.

An authenticated user with permission to create or update `NodeUpgradeJob` resources through the v1alpha2 API could include shell metacharacters in either field. When the upgrade job was processed, the injected command could be executed on the targeted edge node with the privileges available to the upgrade process.

Successful exploitation could result in arbitrary command execution and compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the affected edge node.

## Patches

The fix removes shell-based command construction and invokes `keadm` using a structured argument list through `exec.Command`.

The version and image values are passed as separate literal arguments and are no longer interpreted by a command shell.

The fixed versions:

* KubeEdge v1.23.1
* KubeEdge v1.22.2
* KubeEdge v1.21.2

## Workarounds

Until a patched version is available:

* restrict permission to create or update `NodeUpgradeJob` resources to trusted administrators;
* do not allow untrusted users or tenants to control the `spec.version` or `spec.image` fields;
* avoid using NodeUpgradeJob-based edge upgrades in environments where these fields may be influenced by untrusted users.

## Credits

KubeEdge thanks Sang-Hoon Choi ([KoreaSecurity](https://github.com/KoreaSecurity), Sejong University)
for responsibly reporting this issue and for coordinating with the KubeEdge
maintainers through the security disclosure process.

items.title: KubeEdge: keadm DecompressTarGz path traversal enables arbitrary file write on Windows during edge node join
items.summary:
## Description

KubeEdge `keadm` contains a path traversal vulnerability in the `DecompressTarGz` archive extraction function.

Archive entry names were joined directly with the extraction destination without sufficient validation. A crafted tar.gz archive containing parent-directory components, Windows-style backslashes, absolute paths, or drive-prefixed paths could cause files to be written outside the intended extraction directory.

The issue is particularly relevant to Windows edge nodes during the `keadm join` or installation process when `keadm` extracts downloaded component archives.

## Impact

An attacker who can cause an affected `keadm` process to extract a malicious archive may write or overwrite files outside the intended destination directory with the privileges of the user running `keadm`.

On Windows edge nodes, this may allow modification of configuration files, executable files, service-related files, or other writable system locations. Depending on the overwritten file and the privileges of the `keadm` process, successful exploitation could lead to persistent system modification or code execution.

Exploitation requires the attacker to influence the contents of an archive processed by `keadm`, such as through a compromised, replaced, or otherwise untrusted download source.

## Patches

The extraction logic now:

* resolves the destination directory to an absolute path;
* rejects empty archive entry names;
* normalizes Windows-style path separators before validation;
* rejects parent-directory traversal paths;
* rejects absolute and Windows drive-prefixed paths;
* uses `filepath-securejoin` to ensure extracted files remain within the destination directory.

Fixes are planned for the following maintained releases:

* v1.23.1
* v1.22.2
* v1.21.2

## Workarounds

Until a patched release is available:

* only install or join edge nodes using trusted KubeEdge package sources;
* verify the integrity and origin of downloaded archives before extraction;
* do not use custom or untrusted component archives with `keadm`;
* restrict write permissions and administrative privileges for the account running `keadm`;
* avoid performing Windows edge-node installation or join operations when the package source cannot be trusted.

## Credits

KubeEdge thanks Sang-Hoon Choi ([KoreaSecurity](https://github.com/KoreaSecurity), Sejong University)
for responsibly reporting this issue and for coordinating with the KubeEdge
maintainers through the security disclosure process.

items.title: Dynamic Conformance Testing of WebGPU Through Specification-Driven Mutation
items.summary: WebGPU is a low-level graphics and compute API that exposes modern GPU functionality to web applications. While the official WebGPU Conformance Test Suite (CTS) focuses on well-formed usage under the WebGPU specification, it is not designed to stress implementations with semantic edge cases or adversarial inputs. General-purpose fuzzers, in contrast, struggle with WebGPU because of its complex graphics stack and multi-process architecture. We introduce LANTERN, a specification-guided dynamic conformance testing framework that mutates CTS tests using constraints extracted from the WebGPU specification. LANTERN extracts explicit syntactic API rules from WebIDL definitions and recovers semantic constraints, such as command ordering and object lifetimes, from natural-language specification text. Selected rules guide AST-located textual transformations that generate both valid and intentionally invalid CTS variants. We execute the resulting tests at scale on AddressSanitizer-instrumented Chromium to discover bugs. Our evaluation discovers three reproducible bugs, including a heap corruption, in Chromium versions current at the time of study. These results demonstrate that syntactically seeded, semantics-aware mutation of conformance tests provides a way to uncover browser bugs during WebGPU testing.

llm_summary.summary_zh: 该论文（arXiv, cs.SE）研究的是浏览器中 WebGPU 实现的质量与安全问题。WebGPU 是一项向 Web 应用暴露现代 GPU 能力的低层图形与计算 API，其官方一致性测试套件（CTS）主要验证「符合规范的正常用法」，并不覆盖语义边界情况或对抗性输入；而通用模糊测试器由于 WebGPU 图形栈复杂、包含多进程架构（浏览器进程、GPU 进程、渲染进程之间的 IPC），难以有效触达深层代码路径。为此作者提出 LANTERN —— 一个由规范驱动的动态一致性测试框架。其核心思路是：以现有 CTS 测试为种子，从 WebGPU 规范中抽取约束，并用这些约束来指导变异。具体而言，LANTERN 从 WebIDL 定义中提取显式的语法层 API 规则，同时从自然语言撰写的规范正文中恢复语义约束，例如命令提交顺序、对象生命周期与状态依赖等；随后由选中的规则驱动基于 AST 定位的文本变换，批量生成既包含合法变体、也包含「故意违规」变体的 CTS 测试用例，从而在规模上执行到大体量的边界与非法输入组合。作者在 AddressSanitizer 插桩的 Chromium 上大规模运行这些变体，评估结果显示共发现三个可稳定复现的缺陷，其中包含一处堆内存破坏（heap corruption），且受影响的 Chromium 版本在研究所处的时间点仍为当前版本。论文的主要贡献在于：提出了一条「以语法种子 + 语义感知变异」来增强一致性测试的思路，把规范文本转化为可执行的变异约束，并实证了该方法能够在真实浏览器引擎中发现内存安全类缺陷；同时说明规范驱动的变异可以作为通用 fuzzer 与官方 CTS 之间的补充层。适合浏览器/渲染引擎测试工程师、WebGPU 实现方、以及从事规格驱动测试与编译器/API 变异研究的读者阅读。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: WebGPU 正快速进入生产浏览器，其实现缺陷可能直接导致渲染进程内存破坏。该工作说明官方 CTS 并非安全边界，规范驱动的语义变异能在真实引擎中发现可复现的内存安全缺陷，为浏览器厂商和依赖 WebGPU 的应用方提供了低成本的质量与安全补强思路。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 影响面覆盖 Chromium/WebGPU 实现方、基于 WebGPU 的图形与 AI 推理 Web 应用、以及浏览器自动化与沙箱逃逸研究者；方法论可迁移到其它具有 WebIDL/规范文本的 Web API（如 WebAssembly、WebCodecs、WebAudio）的一致性测试增强与 CI 回归。
detection_signals_zh: 浏览器渲染进程/GPU 进程异常崩溃、SIGSEGV 或堆损坏报告，尤其在大量重复 WebGPU 命令提交、资源创建与销毁交错时
AddressSanitizer / MemorySanitizer 在 CI 中针对 WebGPU 路径报出的 heap-buffer-overflow、use-after-free 类告警
页面侧出现异常数量的 WebGPU 校验错误（validation error）与设备丢失（device lost）事件聚集，可能对应非法命令序列探测
同一页面短时间内高频创建/销毁 GPUDevice、GPUBuffer、GPUCommandEncoder 等对象的可疑时序模式
defense_advice_zh: 将 Chromium 及 WebGPU 实现升级到包含相关修复的最新稳定版，并关注上游安全公告与浏览器版本发布节奏
在浏览器/引擎 CI 中启用 ASan 等内存检查插桩，并将规范驱动的变异测试纳入回归流水线，优先覆盖命令顺序、对象生命周期等语义约束
对 WebGPU 使用方：避免在不可信输入驱动下构造复杂资源生命周期，配合设备错误回调做优雅降级
在托管侧评估是否需要通过企业策略限制或按需启用 WebGPU，降低攻击面，同时保留本地合规业务的可用性
跟踪 W3C WebGPU 规范与 CTS 的更新，把新增语义约束同步到内部测试用例生成规则中
llm_summary.recommended_action_zh: 研究跟进

items.title: CMSimple 5.24 ships with CSRF protection disabled by default, which turns csrfProtection() into a...
items.summary: CMSimple 5.24 ships with CSRF protection disabled by default, which turns csrfProtection() into a no-op on every state-changing admin request, and it does not send the csrf_token hidden field in admin forms. Because administrator authentication is cookie-only and no CSRF token is enforced, an unauthenticated attacker can induce a logged-in administrator's browser to issue a forged content-save request with a text payload containing a scripting marker. The marker is stored verbatim into content/content.php; on every subsequent page view evaluate_cmsimple_scripting() (functions.php) executes the marker body with PHP eval() — for all visitors, including unauthenticated ones. This yields persistent remote code execution on the web server.

items.title: Cloudreve: SSRF guard bypass: checkIP does not decode IPv6-transition wrappers (NAT64, IPv4-compatible, 6to4) reaching internal and cloud-metadata addresses
items.summary:
**Summary**

Cloudreve's server-side request forgery guard `ValidateExternalURL` (`pkg/request/ssrf.go`) resolves a user-supplied URL host and rejects it when any resolved IP is a loopback, private, link-local, multicast, unspecified, CGNAT, or the cloud-metadata address. The classification is performed by `checkIP`, which uses Go's `net.IP` builtins (`IsLoopback`, `IsPrivate`, `IsLinkLocalUnicast`, ...) directly on the resolved address. These builtins inspect only the outer IPv6 address and do not decode IPv4-in-IPv6 transition wrappers. An attacker who controls a hostname's AAAA record (or, on a DNS64/NAT64 network, any hostname) can point the remote-download URL at a NAT64 well-known-prefix address (`64:ff9b::a.b.c.d`, RFC 6052), an IPv4-compatible address (`::a.b.c.d`, RFC 4291), or a 6to4 address (`2002:AABB:CCDD::`, RFC 3056) that wraps an internal IPv4. Go classifies these wrappers as ordinary global IPv6 addresses, so `checkIP` accepts them; the network then delivers the request to the embedded internal IPv4 (loopback, RFC 1918, or the cloud instance metadata service `169.254.169.254`). This bypasses the SSRF guard that was added to block direct access to internal services.

**Affected component and versions**

- Component: `pkg/request/ssrf.go` (`ValidateExternalURL` / `checkIP`), reached from the remote-download workflow `pkg/filemanager/workflows/remote_download.go` (`RemoteDownloadTask.createDownloadTask`, which passes the user-supplied `SrcUri` to `ValidateExternalURL`).
- Affected: Cloudreve `<= 4.17.0` (latest release at time of report) and current `main`.
- Reachable by an authenticated remote-download user; administrative privileges are not required.

**Vulnerable form vs correctly-guarded sibling**

`checkIP` DOES block IPv4-mapped IPv6 (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`), because Go's `net.IP.To4()` returns the embedded IPv4 for that form and the standard checks then fire. It does NOT block the other IPv4-in-IPv6 transition forms, because for those `To4()` returns nil and every `net.IP` classifier reports the wrapper as a normal global IPv6 address:

- NAT64 well-known prefix `64:ff9b::/96` (RFC 6052): `64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe` embeds `169.254.169.254`.
- IPv4-compatible `::a.b.c.d` (RFC 4291): `::a9fe:a9fe` embeds `169.254.169.254`.
- 6to4 `2002::/16` (RFC 3056): `2002:a9fe:a9fe::` embeds `169.254.169.254`.

The fix is to canonicalize the resolved address to its embedded IPv4 before classification, symmetric to how IPv4-mapped addresses are already handled by `To4()`. The same gap was fixed correctly in a sibling project: `makeplane/plane` `apps/api/plane/utils/ip_address.py` `_embedded_ipv4()` decodes IPv4-mapped, 6to4, Teredo and NAT64 before classifying; Cloudreve's guard is the unpatched twin of that pattern.

**Severity**

An authenticated low-privilege user can force the server to fetch attacker-chosen internal URLs and read the responses, including cloud instance-metadata credentials, producing a scope change from the download subsystem to the internal network and the host's cloud identity. 

**Proof of concept**

The guard file `pkg/request/ssrf.go` imports only the Go standard library, so `ValidateExternalURL` was compiled and called verbatim from tag `4.17.0`. The remote-download workflow calls it as `ValidateExternalURL(ctx, SrcUri, opt)` with default options.

items.title: Spree: Broken Access Control in `PATCH /api/v3/store/carts/:id/associate` (IDOR)
items.summary:
## Summary

The Store API v3 endpoint `PATCH /api/v3/store/carts/:id/associate` binds a guest cart to the authenticated caller without verifying possession of that cart. It locates the cart by prefixed ID only — `current_store.carts.where(user: [nil, current_user]).find_by_prefix_id!(params[:id])` — and omits the `authorize!(:update, @cart, cart_token)` check that every other action in the controller performs via `CartResolvable`. Because prefixed IDs are a reversible Sqids encoding of the auto-increment primary key (obfuscation, not a token), an authenticated customer can name arbitrary guest cart IDs, take them over, and read the checkout addresses stored on them. This is broken access control / IDOR, reachable by any low-privilege registered user.

## Severity

Requires an authenticated store account and depends on target guest carts already carrying an address and not yet being associated, on a store not running in `login_required` mode. Confidentiality impact is the driver (guest checkout PII); integrity impact is limited and recoverable (cart reassignment + email overwrite on an in-progress cart). Not Critical: the action is gated behind authentication (`PR:L`, not `PR:N`) and constrained by cart state, so it is not anonymously exploitable.

## Details

**Root cause:** `associate` skips the cart-possession check its sibling actions enforce and trusts a guessable identifier as the sole locator.

**Entry point.** `Spree::Api::V3::Store::CartsController#associate` (`carts_controller.rb:88-96`), guarded only by `prepend_before_action :require_authentication!, only: [:index, :associate]`. That requires the *caller* be authenticated; it does not tie the request to a specific guest cart.

```ruby
# spree/api/app/controllers/spree/api/v3/store/carts_controller.rb:88-96
# PATCH /api/v3/store/carts/:id/associate
def associate
  @cart = find_cart_for_association

  result = Spree.cart_associate_service.call(guest_order: @cart, user: current_user, guest_only: true)

  if result.success?
    render_cart
  else
    render_service_error(result.error.to_s)
  end
end
```

**Missing check.** `find_cart_for_association` (`carts_controller.rb:177-178`) resolves any guest cart (`user IS NULL`) in the store by ID with no `authorize!(..., cart_token)`. Contrast `CartResolvable#find_cart!`, which binds the token.

```ruby
# spree/api/app/controllers/spree/api/v3/store/carts_controller.rb:177-178
def find_cart_for_association
  current_store.carts.where(user: [nil, current_user]).find_by_prefix_id!(params[:id])
end
```

**Identifier.** `prefixed_id` is `"cart_" + SQIDS.encode([id])` with `SQIDS = Sqids.new(min_length: 10)` (`prefixed_id.rb:17,56`) — default alphabet, no salt, no blocklist. Sqids is non-cryptographic and reversible, so candidate IDs are derivable offline from sequential primary keys.

```ruby
# spree/core/app/models/concerns/spree/prefixed_id.rb:17-56
SQIDS = Sqids.new(min_length: 10)

def prefixed_id
  return nil unless id.present?

  "#{self.class._prefix_id_prefix}_#{Spree::PrefixedId::SQIDS.encode([id])}"
end
```

**Data flow.** `Spree.cart_associate_service.call(guest_order: @cart, user: current_user, guest_only: true)` reassigns the owner and overwrites email, preserving existing addresses via `bill_address ||= / ship_address ||=`. `render_cart` then serializes `billing_address`/`shipping_address` (first_name, last_name, address1, address2, city, postal_code, phone, company) back to the caller.

## PoC

**Preconditions:** attacker holds an ordinary store account (self-service registration) and the store's publishable key (a front-end credential, present in any headless storefront bundle); one or more guest carts carry checkout addresses; store is not in `login_required` mode.

1. Authenticate: `POST /api/v3/store/auth/login` → attacker JWT.
2. Derive candidate IDs offline: `"cart_" + Sqids.encode([n])` for a range of `n`.
3. For each candidate: `PATCH /api/v3/store/carts/<id>/associate` with the attacker JWT. A hit returns

items.title: Nautobot: Stored cross-site scripting (XSS) in object create/edit form help text
items.summary:
### Impact
_What kind of vulnerability is it? Who is impacted?_

It has two related instances that share the same root cause: a user-controlled model field is assigned verbatim to a form field's `help_text`, which is rendered with Django's `|safe` filter (`render_field.html`), bypassing auto-escaping.

In both cases the script executes in the browser of any user who opens an affected create or edit form, **including administrators and superusers**. Because the payload runs in the victim's authenticated session, it can lead to actions performed as the victim, session/token theft, and further privilege escalation. Exploitation requires the victim to open an affected form.

#### Relationship description

A user who holds the add/change permission for Relationships (`extras.add_relationship` / `extras.change_relationship`) can set a Relationship's **description** to an HTML/JavaScript payload. That description is used as the help text of the relationship's form field and is rendered on the create/edit page of every object type the relationship applies to.

#### Module Family name

A user who holds the add/change permission for Module Families (`dcim.add_modulefamily` / `dcim.change_modulefamily`) can put a payload in a Module Family **name**, which is interpolated into the `module_family` field's help text on the Module "Install module" form for any module bay assigned to that family.

### Patches
_Has the problem been patched? What versions should users upgrade to?_

Fixes are available in Nautobot v2.4.37+ & v3.1.8+

> Note: The underlying weakness exists in earlier EOL versions of Nautobot (v1.x). Users on those older EOL versions are highly encouraged to upgrade to a supported version.

### Workarounds
_Is there a way for users to fix or remediate the vulnerability without upgrading?_

There is no configuration-only fix. To remediate without upgrading:

- Restrict the `extras.add_relationship` / `extras.change_relationship` and `dcim.add_modulefamily` / `dcim.change_modulefamily` permissions to fully trusted administrators only.
- Audit existing Relationship **description** values and Module Family **name** values for embedded HTML / `<script>` content and remove any payloads.

Note that limiting who can open create/edit forms does not fully mitigate the issue, since the payload targets any user (including admins) who opens an affected form.

### Credit

Credit for this discovery goes to Habibullo Izzatilloyev.

items.title: Autobahn Python permessage-deflate bypasses maxMessagePayloadSize after inflation
items.summary:
### Summary
Autobahn Python enforces `maxMessagePayloadSize` against the compressed WebSocket frame length before permessage-deflate inflation, then delivers the inflated message to application callbacks without a second size check. A client frame that is only 22 compressed bytes can inflate to 4096 bytes and reach `onMessage` even when the application configured a 128-byte message limit, defeating the resource boundary the option is meant to provide.

### Details
The permessage-deflate path installs a `PerMessageDeflate` instance when the server accepts a client offer in `src/autobahn/websocket/protocol.py:3371`. The common `PerMessageDeflateOfferAccept(offer)` path leaves `max_message_size` at its default `None` in `src/autobahn/websocket/compress_deflate.py:295`, and that value is copied into the compressor object in `src/autobahn/websocket/compress_deflate.py:723`. When a data frame arrives with RSV1 set, Autobahn marks the message compressed in `src/autobahn/websocket/protocol.py:1812`, calls `onMessageFrameBegin` with the compressed frame length, and increments `message_data_total_length` by that pre-inflate length in `src/autobahn/websocket/protocol.py:634`; the configured message cap is enforced against the same compressed accounting at `src/autobahn/websocket/protocol.py:636`. Only after those checks does Autobahn inflate the payload in `src/autobahn/websocket/protocol.py:1861`; because `max_message_size` is `None`, `src/autobahn/websocket/compress_deflate.py:812` calls zlib without an output cap. The inflated bytes are then passed to `onMessageFrameData` in `src/autobahn/websocket/protocol.py:1882`, appended for WebSocket version 13 without adding their inflated length to the message counter at `src/autobahn/websocket/protocol.py:667`, joined in `src/autobahn/websocket/protocol.py:690`, and delivered through `_onMessage` in `src/autobahn/websocket/protocol.py:693`. items.title: POZZER: A Power Side Channel-guided Fuzzer for Black-Box Embedded Systems
items.summary: Firmware fuzzing is an effective technique for discovering vulnerabilities in embedded systems. However, existing coverage-guided firmware fuzzers typically obtain feedback through firmware instrumentation, hardware debug interfaces, or firmware rehosting, which requires access to the firmware source code or binary image. Such requirements are often infeasible for off-the-shelf embedded devices, where firmware binaries are inaccessible, unrehostable, immodifiable, or undebuggable, necessitating fuzzing under black-box conditions. In this paper, we present POZZER, a power side-channel-guided fuzzer for black-box embedded systems. POZZER uses power traces as feedback to identify previously unseen behavior via an incrementally constructed graph-based representation of observed executions, guiding the fuzzer toward unexplored execution paths. Its non-profiling design requires neither prior firmware knowledge nor a clone device, extracting meaningful feedback from a single power trace per execution while remaining robust to measurement noise. We evaluate POZZER on 15 firmware targets across two platforms and two real-world commercial embedded devices. Across the resulting target-platform combinations, POZZER outperforms a blind fuzzer under the same time budget in 26 out of 30 target-platform combinations. Furthermore, POZZER discovers two previously unknown vulnerabilities in one of the commercial devices, both confirmed by the vendor, demonstrating its potential for identifying vulnerabilities in black-box embedded systems.

llm_summary.summary_zh: 该论文针对嵌入式系统固件漏洞挖掘中的黑盒难题提出了 POZZER——一种以功耗侧信道为反馈的模糊测试器。传统覆盖引导的固件模糊测试通常依赖固件插桩、硬件调试接口或固件重宿主(rehosting)来获取执行反馈, 这些手段都以能够访问固件源码或二进制镜像为前提。然而在真实场景中, 大量商用设备属于"不可获取二进制、不可重宿主、不可修改、不可调试"的四不可状态
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 大量物联网/工控设备固件不可获取、不可重宿主, 传统覆盖引导模糊测试无从下手。该工作证明仅靠功耗侧信道即可在黑盒条件下引导模糊测试并挖出厂商确认的真实漏洞, 为硬件安全评估与固件供应链审计提供了可借鉴的新反馈通道。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 可迁移至消费级物联网设备、工业控制器、车规 ECU 等固件封闭或调试口被锁的场景; 对具备物理接触或近场功耗采集能力的渗透测试、设备准入评估与第三方固件安全审计流程有参考价值; 也可能被用于绕过"无源码不测试"的评估盲区。
detection_signals_zh: 目标设备供电轨出现异常的高频纹波或电流波动, 疑似外接功耗采集探针
设备在短时间内被反复复位、掉电重启并注入异常输入, 呈现模糊测试特征
调试接口/电源引脚被物理接入外部测量设备, 或外壳被拆解
设备运行时出现非预期的异常崩溃、看门狗复位或错误日志集中爆发
defense_advice_zh: 对关键嵌入式设备实施物理防护: 封胶、防拆开关、调试口熔断与安全启动, 提升黑盒功耗采集的获取门槛
在电源与时钟设计中加入稳压、滤波与噪声注入, 降低功耗轨迹的可分析性
部署固件运行时完整性校验与异常复位/崩溃遥测, 用于发现设备被反复测试的迹象
在采购与准入环节要求厂商提供固件 SBOM 与漏洞响应流程, 对不可审计固件设备进行风险评估
llm_summary.recommended_action_zh: 研究跟进

items.title: State-Aware Fuzzing of JavaScript Engines with LLM-Guided Instrumentation
items.summary: The security of the modern web depends on the correctness of JavaScript (JS) engines, yet these complex systems remain vulnerable to high-impact bugs. A critical limitation of state-of-the-art fuzzers is the coverage plateau: once a fuzzer saturates the control-flow graph, edge coverage loses its ability to guide discovery. Because complex engine behaviors, such as JIT optimization tiers and hidden class transitions, often share identical edge coverage, standard coverage metrics are blind to the distinct internal states required to trigger deep errors. To bridge this gap, we present StateLens, a framework that employs Large Language Models (LLM) to automate the discovery of deep internal states. Blindly placing instrumentation probes at all states is infeasible due to the vast state space and the high runtime overhead. StateLens introduces a novel agent-based reasoning pipeline that emulates the intuition of a security researcher. By iteratively traversing code and developer comments, our agents intelligently select high-value instrumentation targets, effectively separating logic-driving state variables from irrelevant data. This results in synthesizable, high-signal feedback probes that map the engine's hidden configurations. This instrumentation feeds a dual-feedback mechanism, effectively guiding the fuzzer toward unexplored engine semantics. Our evaluation confirms that StateLens significantly outperforms state-of-the-art fuzzers and uncovering 68 new bugs.

llm_summary.summary_zh: 该论文针对 JavaScript 引擎模糊测试中的“覆盖率平台期”问题提出了名为 StateLens 的框架。背景是：现代 Web 安全高度依赖 JS 引擎的正确性，而引擎本身极其复杂，仍不断暴露高危缺陷。当前最先进的模糊测试器主要依赖边覆盖率（edge coverage）作为反馈信号，但一旦控制流图被基本覆盖，边覆盖率就失去了指导能力，测试进入平台期。作者指出根本原因在于：JS 引擎中大量语义上截然不同的内部行为——例如 JIT 优化层级切换、隐藏类（hidden class）转换等——在边覆盖层面表现完全相同，因此标准覆盖率指标对触发深层错误所必需的内部状态“视而不见”。为解决这一问题，StateLens 使用大语言模型（LLM）自动发现引擎的深层内部状态。由于引擎状态空间极为庞大，且插桩会带来高昂运行时开销，无法在所有状态点盲目布设探针。为此作者设计了一条新颖的、基于智能体（agent）的推理流水线，模拟安全研究员的直觉：智能体迭代地遍历源代码与开发者注释，评估并挑出高价值插桩目标，将真正驱动逻辑的状态变量与无关数据区分开来，最终合成出高信号的反馈探针，用于刻画引擎的隐藏配置空间。这些插桩产生的状态反馈与传统的边覆盖率结合，形成“双反馈”机制，引导模糊测试器进入此前从未探索的引擎语义区域。评估结果表明，StateLens 显著优于当前最先进的模糊测试器，并新发现 68 个缺陷。整体而言，该工作把 LLM 智能体从“代码生成/漏洞识别”扩展到了“测试基础设施增强”这一新用途，为状态敏感的模糊测试提供了可借鉴的自动化插桩范式，适合引擎安全、编译器/运行时、模糊测试与 LLM 智能体方向的研究者与工程团队阅读。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 边覆盖率饱和是主流模糊测试器的共性瓶颈，该工作用 LLM 智能体自动挑选高价值状态插桩点，把“不可见”的引擎内部状态变成可用反馈信号，为提升 JIT 类复杂运行时的缺陷发现效率提供了可迁移的新思路。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 可迁移到 V8/SpiderMonkey/JavaScriptCore 等 JS 引擎、其他带 JIT 或多层状态机的运行时（WASM 引擎、数据库查询引擎、解释器与虚拟机）的模糊测试与回归测试流水线，也可能提升内部安全测试对深层逻辑缺陷的覆盖能力。
detection_signals_zh: 自动化构建/测试环境中出现由 LLM 智能体驱动的插桩点选择或探针代码生成流程
模糊测试过程中出现自定义状态反馈指标与边覆盖率并用的双反馈调度特征
测试目标集中在 JS 引擎 JIT 优化层级切换、隐藏类转换等内部状态相关代码路径
defense_advice_zh: 关注团队自有 JS/运行时目标的覆盖率平台期现象，评估引入状态反馈指标补充边覆盖率的可行性
在内部引擎安全测试流程中试点 LLM 辅助的插桩目标筛选，但需对生成探针做人工评审与性能回归验证
对新增的状态探针建立运行时开销与稳定性基线，避免因插桩过重影响持续 fuzzing 吞吐
跟踪该工作开源实现（若有）并在隔离环境中评估后再纳入生产测试链路
llm_summary.recommended_action_zh: 研究跟进：阅读原文与评估细节，评估其状态插桩与双反馈机制在自有运行时/引擎测试中的可迁移性

items.title: Rouxii: Exploiting Honeypots with Deception-Aware AI Pentesters
items.summary: Honeypots are designed to deceive attackers, and recent work shows they can also derail autonomous LLM-based pentesters. These evaluations, however, largely consider attackers unaware of the deception they face. We study the opposite setting: an autonomous attacker explicitly equipped to recognize and act on honeypot fingerprints. We introduce Rouxii, an AI-driven penetration-testing framework that integrates counter-deception into reconnaissance and pivots from honeypot detection to exploitation. We evaluate matched vanilla and anti-deception Rouxii configurations across three reasoning models and eleven network setups over twelve cycles (1,544 attack reports). Between the matched cohorts, which differ only in the prompt, counter-deception raises correct honeypot identification from 19% to 97%, an effect strongest on OT services (11% to 97%), while false alarms on the real service stay at 0.7%. Deception-unaware baselines (PentestGPT, HackingBuddy) fail similarly, indicating the effect is not specific to our framework. Detection, moreover, is not the endpoint: through a white-box analysis of the honeypots themselves we show that a detected trap can be turned against its operator, demonstrating a denial-of-service that disables Conpot without tripping its liveness monitoring, and a corruption of the intelligence a GasPot instance reports. These findings show that deception effectiveness depends strongly on attacker knowledge, and that evaluations of honeypot resilience against AI attackers must account for adversaries that actively reason about and exploit the deception layer.

llm_summary.summary_zh: 蜜罐的设计目标是欺骗攻击者，近期研究还发现蜜罐能够扰乱基于 LLM 的自主渗透测试智能体。然而，这类评测几乎都建立在同一个隐含前提上：攻击者并不知道自己正面对欺骗环境。本文研究的是相反的设定——攻击者被显式地赋予识别蜜罐指纹并据此行动的能力。作者提出 Rouxii，一个 AI 驱动的渗透测试框架，把反欺骗能力整合进侦察阶段，并支持从「发现蜜罐」转向「利用蜜罐」。实验设计上，作者在三种推理模型、十一种网络拓扑配置、十二个攻击周期下，对 vanilla 配置与反欺骗配置进行配对对比，共计收集 1,544 份攻击报告。两个队列之间唯一的差异是提示词。结果显示，加入反欺骗能力后，正确识别蜜罐的比例从 19% 提升到 97%；在 OT（运营技术）类服务上效果最显著，从 11% 提升到 97%；与此同时，对真实服务产生的误报率仍保持在 0.7% 的低水平。作者还测试了不具备欺骗意识的基线工具 PentestGPT 和 HackingBuddy，它们在同类任务上同样失败，说明这种脆弱性并非 Rouxii 框架特有，而是更普遍的问题。更重要的是，识别蜜罐并不是终点：通过对蜜罐软件本体的白盒分析，作者证明被识破的陷阱可以被反向用来对付其运营方，包括在不触发存活监控的情况下使 Conpot 实例失去可用性，以及污染 GasPot 实例所上报的情报数据。整体结论是：欺骗手段的有效性高度依赖攻击者的知识水平，而评估蜜罐对 AI 攻击者的韧性时，必须把「会主动推理并利用欺骗层」的对手纳入考量。该工作适合蜜罐/欺骗防御研究者、威胁情报平台建设者、OT 安全团队以及使用 LLM 智能体做对抗仿真的红队阅读。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 它直接挑战了欺骗防御的默认假设：一旦 AI 智能体能识别蜜罐指纹，蜜罐的识别率会从 19% 跃升到 97%，且被识破的蜜罐可被反制——导致 liveness 监控失效的不可用状态，以及上报情报被污染。防御方若只用蜜罐作为主要情报来源，需重新评估数据可信度与自身存活监控的可靠性。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 影响面覆盖欺骗防御体系与基于蜜罐的威胁情报供给链：当部署 Conpot、GasPot 等常见开源蜜罐时，其可用性与上报数据完整性可能被有欺骗意识的 AI 攻击者削弱；同时，依赖蜜罐数据做检测规则、IOC 富化的 SOC 流程会因情报污染而误判。可迁移到任何使用 LLM 智能体做自动化红队/对抗仿真的场景，用于评估自家蜜罐在「知情的 AI 对手」面前的韧性。
detection_signals_zh: 蜜罐进程（如 Conpot）对外不再正常响应，但主机与应用存活心跳、外部监控探针仍显示正常，二者出现不一致
蜜罐实例上报的情报数据出现统计上异常、内部逻辑不自洽或与独立传感器结果背离的条目
对蜜罐指纹特征（默认配置、banner、响应时序、协议实现细节）出现高密度、系统化的探测与验证行为
自动化智能体特征流量：大量结构化、多轮迭代的侦察请求，节奏与人类操作显著不同
同一来源在识别出蜜罐后，访问行为从探测转为针对蜜罐软件本身的异常交互
蜜罐集群中出现单点或多个实例同时进入「静默但不告警」状态的模式
defense_advice_zh: 不要仅依赖蜜罐自身的存活监控，需增加带外独立心跳与外部探针校验，避免监控被绕过而无人察觉
将蜜罐产出视为低可信度信号，与独立传感器、端点日志、网络流量分析交叉验证后再用于检测与情报
对蜜罐上报数据做完整性与合理性校验（schema、频率、统计基线），发现异常条目时及时隔离并标记
提升蜜罐指纹的隐蔽性与多样性，减少默认模板与可指纹化特征，降低被自动化识别与针对性利用的概率
把「知情的 AI 对手」纳入红队评估范围，用具备反欺骗能力的 LLM 智能体对自有蜜罐进行对抗性验证
针对 OT 类蜜罐（如 Modbus/工业协议仿真）单独评估风险，因该类服务在本文中识别率提升幅度最大、最易被攻破
为蜜罐环境配置严格的隔离与资源限制，避免其被反制后影响同一网络中的其他资产

items.title: C-to-Rust Fallacy: Automatic Refactoring != Memory Security
items.summary: Rust has emerged as the leading system programming language, offering strong memory and type safety guarantees without compromising performance. This positions it as a compelling alternative to traditional languages like C and C++, which are susceptible to memory security bugs. However, manually transforming C to Rust requires in-depth domain knowledge of the Rust language features, which requires significant effort for developers. To address this, tools for automatic C-to-Rust refactoring aim to generate safe Rust code leveraging static analysis and Large Language Models (LLMs). While these tools claim to achieve safety by reducing the unsafe Rust, the correlation with improving security is not clear. In this paper, we conduct a comprehensive empirical study on the reliability, safety, and correctness of various C-to-Rust refactoring methods. Specifically, we evaluate C2Rust-analyze, CROWN, C2SaferRust, and FLOURINE using a dataset of 116 C programs with memory security bugs from the NIST Juliet Test Suite. Based on 464 Rust programs generated by these tools, our evaluation focuses on three key aspects: the compilation correctness of the refactored programs, the effectiveness in mitigating original C bugs, and the tendency to introduce additional Rust bugs. The results indicate that 342 Rust programs fail to compile, 177 Rust programs inherit memory security bugs from the original C programs, and 77 new Rust bugs are introduced. We examine the rationale behind tool design and analyze the root cause of errors across various refactoring methods. Our findings indicate that current automated refactoring tools deliver memory safety as they define it, but not the broader memory security when adopting them.

llm_summary.summary_zh:
该论文针对当前兴起的“自动将 C 代码重构为 Rust 以消除内存安全缺陷”的做法提出了批判性实证评估。研究背景是：Rust 凭借编译期的内存与类型安全保证、且不牺牲性能，被广泛视为 C/C++ 的替代方案；但人工把 C 迁移到 Rust 需要深入掌握 Rust 的语言特性与所有权模型，成本极高。为此，业界出现了 C2Rust-analyze、CROWN、C2SaferRust、FLOURINE 等自动重构工具，它们结合静态分析与大语言模型（LLM）生成 Rust 代码，并以“减少 unsafe Rust 代码”作为实现安全性的证据。作者指出，这种“unsafe 代码变少”与“程序真正变安全”之间并没有被验证的因果关系，因此系统性地考察了多种 C-to-Rust 重构方法的可靠性、安全性与正确性。

实验设计上，作者从 NIST Juliet Test Suite 中挑选了 116 个包含内存安全缺陷的 C 程序，分别交给上述四种工具处理，共生成 464 个 Rust 程序。评估围绕三个维度展开：一是重构后程序的编译正确性；二是对原始 C 缺陷的消除效果；三是是否引入新的 Rust 缺陷。结果显示：342 个 Rust 程序无法编译；177 个 Rust 程序仍继承原 C 程序的内存安全缺陷；另有 77 个新的 Rust 缺陷被引入。作者进一步剖析了各工具的设计理念，并对不同重构方法的错误根因进行了归类分析。

论文的核心结论是：现有自动重构工具确实能够实现它们自己定义意义上的“内存安全”（例如减少 unsafe 块），但并不能实现更广义的“内存安全（security）”——即真正消除可利用的内存安全漏洞。该工作揭示了“自动重构等于内存安全”这一假设的谬误，提醒业界在把 C 迁移到 Rust 作为安全加固手段时，必须引入独立的验证与审计，而不能仅凭工具宣称的安全指标。适合 Rust 迁移项目负责人、安全工程与代码审计人员、以及研究程序语言与安全交叉方向的读者阅读。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 许多团队正把 C-to-Rust 自动重构当作内存安全漏洞的根治手段。该研究用 116 个带缺陷程序、4 种工具、464 个产物证明：大量结果无法编译、仍带原有缺陷、还会引入新缺陷。安全从业者不能把“unsafe 代码减少”等同于漏洞消除，必须对重构产物做独立验证。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 影响所有计划或正在用自动工具把 C/C++ 迁移到 Rust 的项目，包括遗留系统加固、嵌入式与系统软件供应链、以及以 Rust 重写作为漏洞修复策略的安全团队；也适用于评估 LLM 辅助代码迁移在安全关键场景中的可信边界。
detection_signals_zh: 重构产物编译失败率异常偏高
Rust 代码中仍残留原 C 缺陷对应的逻辑模式
新引入的 Rust 缺陷（如越界、未检查索引、错误的所有权转换）
为通过编译而保留或新增的 unsafe 块与外部函数接口调用
defense_advice_zh: 不要把自动 C-to-Rust 重构直接作为漏洞修复的最终交付，需配套独立的安全验证
对重构产物强制执行编译、单元测试、静态分析与模糊测试
保留原始 C 程序的缺陷清单，做逐条回归确认缺陷已被真实消除
重点审计残留 unsafe 块、FFI 边界和由工具自动插入的类型转换
在迁移流程中引入人工代码审查与 Rust 安全专家复核

items.title: The Price of Safety: Benign-Case Utility and Token Overhead of Memory-Poisoning Defenses in LLM Agents
items.summary: Memory-poisoning defenses for LLM agents are typically evaluated by their ability to prevent attacks. However, the traffic they process is rarely adversarial. The cost of implementing a defense is paid with each interaction, while its benefits are only seen in a small percentage of cases. We developed a measurement setup that keeps the memory backend, retrieval process, and judge consistent across different conditions, changing only the defense itself. We test each condition three times across five conversations to distinguish the defense's real effects from noise inherent in the pipeline's runs, which remains significant even at temperature zero. Across three write-time defenses (input sanitization, provenance checking, and LLM-based anomaly detection) and one read-time defense (reranking), tested on entirely benign traffic, the write-time defenses show no utility cost we can resolve, with 95% confidence intervals spanning roughly +/-4.5 points and including zero. The reranker is different: it lowers core accuracy by 4.4 points (95% CI [-9.0,-0.05], bootstrap; McNemar p=0.064), a result that survives replication but sits at the edge of our resolution. Its clearer cost is mechanical rather than statistical. On conversations containing no attack, the reranker quarantines legitimate memories on 33.6% of adjudicated items, reaching as many as 106 false quarantines in a single conversation, at 2.7% token overhead. Stacking all four defenses does not compound this cost: the combined condition's accuracy loss is smaller, and its confidence interval includes zero, suggesting the write-time defenses may partly offset what the reranker discards. Where a defense intercepts the pipeline, not whether it uses an LLM, appears to determine its benign-case price.

llm_summary.summary_zh: 该论文研究了一个在 LLM 智能体安全中常被忽视的问题：记忆投毒防御在【良性流量】下的实用性与 token 开销。作者指出，现有记忆投毒防御通常只按“能否阻止攻击”来评估，但真实线上流量极少是恶意的；防御的实现成本却是每一次交互都要支付，而收益只在极少数攻击场景中体现。为此，作者设计了一套测量装置，保持记忆后端、检索流程与判定器（judge）在不同实验条件之间完全一致，唯一变量是所启用的防御本身。为避免流水线固有噪声（即使在 temperature=0 时噪声依然显著）干扰结论，作者在 5 段对话上对每种条件重复测试 3 次，以区分防御的真实效果与随机波动。实验覆盖三类写时防御（输入净化、来源/溯源检查、基于 LLM 的异常检测）和一类读时防御（重排序 reranking），全部在完全良性的流量上进行。结果显示：三类写时防御没有可分辨的实用性代价，其 95% 置信区间约为 ±4.5 个点且包含零。读时重排序防御则不同，核心准确率下降 4.4 个点（95% CI [-9.0,-0.05]，bootstrap；McNemar p=0.064），该结果可复现但处于测量分辨率边缘。重排序更明确的代价是机制性的而非统计性的：在完全不含攻击的对话中，它在 33.6% 的待裁决条目上隔离了合法记忆，单段对话最多出现 106 次误隔离，并带来约 2.7% 的 token 开销。作者还发现，四种防御全部堆叠并不会导致成本叠加：组合条件的准确率损失反而更小，且置信区间包含零，这暗示写时防御可能部分抵消了重排序所丢弃的信息。最终结论是：防御在流水线中的拦截位置（写时还是读时），而不是它是否使用 LLM，似乎决定了其在良性场景下的代价。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 安全团队在 LLM 智能体上部署记忆投毒防御时，往往只关注攻击拦截率，却忽略防御对良性业务流的持续损耗。本文给出了可复现的测量方法，提示读时重排序类防御可能大量误伤合法记忆并引入 token 成本，直接影响智能体可用性与运营预算。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 可迁移到所有带长期记忆或 RAG 检索的 LLM 智能体系统，尤其是需要在生产流量中评估防御实用性、误隔离率与 token 开销的团队；也可用于防御方案选型与堆叠策略验证。
detection_signals_zh: 无攻击对话中合法记忆被隔离的比例异常升高（如超过三成）
单次会话中出现大量同类型记忆隔离事件（可达上百次）
每轮交互 token 消耗相对基线上升约 2% 至 3%
读时重排序组件触发频率与核心任务准确率下降同时出现
defense_advice_zh: 在良性流量上对防御做 A/B 或重复实验评估，避免只看攻击拦截率
对读时重排序类防御重点监控误隔离率与 token 开销
堆叠多种防御时需验证成本是否叠加或相互抵消，不能默认叠加更安全
在 temperature=0 下也应重复运行以区分防御真实效果与流水线噪声
保留隔离决策的审计记录，便于回溯误伤合法记忆的情况

items.title: Decoding the Legalese: A Scalable and Quantitative Framework for Analyzing Corporate Privacy Policies
items.summary: Even though privacy policies are the primary mechanism organizations use to disclose how they collect, process, and share personal data, they are difficult for average users to interpret, perhaps by design, due to their verbosity and dense legal language. Importantly, there is a lack of standardized metrics that characterize key qualities of a privacy policy beyond regulatory requirements. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) make it feasible to automatically structure and analyze these documents at scale. In this study, we develop and evaluate an end-to-end, LLM-enabled system that converts raw privacy policies into fine-grained structured representations and a set of quantitative measures. Our pipeline applies a detailed taxonomy to extract specific data elements and governing practices, capturing relational links that connect each practice to the data elements it references. We apply our framework to a diverse corpus of 10,000 website privacy policies, yielding, to the best of our knowledge, the most comprehensive dataset of its kind to date. Building on our structured representations, we introduce the first standardized and repeatable quantitative metrics for evaluating privacy policies along four dimensions: completeness, transparency, commitment to user protection, and emphasis on business-driven data practices. This allows us to compare policies within and across industry sectors, and to assess the tension between user protection and business interests.

llm_summary.summary_zh:
隐私政策是各类组织向用户披露其如何收集、处理与共享个人数据的主要机制,但受制于篇幅冗长与法律术语密集的表述方式(论文暗示这可能是刻意为之),普通用户几乎无法真正理解其内容。更关键的是,除监管合规要求之外,业界长期缺乏能够刻画隐私政策关键质量的标准化度量,导致政策之间难以横向比较,也难以判断其真实保护水平。近年来大语言模型(LLM)能力的提升,使得对这类非结构化法律文本进行大规模自动结构化与量化分析成为可能。

针对这一空白,作者开发并系统评估了一套端到端、由 LLM 驱动的分析系统,目标是把原始隐私政策文本转化为细粒度的结构化表示,并在此基础上产出一组可计算的量化指标。其技术路线的核心是:首先定义一套详细的分类法(taxonomy),用于抽取政策中涉及的具体数据元素(如位置、生物特征、支付信息等)以及治理实践(如收集、共享、出售、保留等);其次,在抽取过程中捕获关系链接,把每一项治理实践与其所引用的具体数据元素关联起来,从而形成一个带关系结构的政策知识表示,而非简单的关键词或段落标注。

作者将该框架应用于一个包含 10,000 个网站隐私政策的多样化语料库,构建出据作者所知目前同类中规模最大、覆盖面最广的隐私政策结构化数据集。基于这一表示,论文进一步提出首个标准化、可重复的量化评估体系,沿四个维度刻画隐私政策:完整性(是否充分披露数据实践)、透明度(披露的清晰与可理解程度)、对用户保护的承诺程度,以及对商业驱动型数据实践的强调程度。这四个维度共同构成了一个可比较的隐私政策“仪表盘”,使得既能在同一行业内部,也能跨行业对不同组织的政策进行对比分析,并量化考察用户保护诉求与商业利益诉求之间的张力。

主要贡献可归纳为三点:一是提出可规模化的 LLM 结构化抽取管线与配套分类法,并保留实践—数据元素的关系链接;二是发布万级规模的政策结构化数据集,为后续研究提供基准;三是首次给出标准化、可复现的隐私政策量化指标与四维评估框架。适合隐私与数据治理研究者、企业合规与法务团队、安全与隐私工程师、监管科技从业者以及关注 LLM 在公共政策文本分析中应用的读者阅读。需注意,该系统能力高度依赖 LLM 抽取的准确性与分类法覆盖度,相关偏差与时效性问题在原文中是否得到充分评估,仅凭摘要尚无法确认。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 隐私政策是数据治理透明度的核心披露载体,却长期缺少可量化、可复现的度量标准。该工作把 LLM 结构化抽取与标准化指标结合,使隐私政策审查、行业横向对比、用户保护与商业利益的权衡从人工逐条判读转为可规模化量测,对隐私工程、合规审计与监管科技具有直接的方法学参考价值。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 可迁移到隐私合规审计与供应商尽调、企业数据治理与政策自评平台、监管科技中的政策比对、浏览器或应用商店的隐私评级等场景;其四维指标(完整性、透明度、用户保护承诺、商业实践强调度)可作为组织内部隐私政策质量基线的候选参考。局限在于依赖 LLM 抽取,存在模型偏差、分类法覆盖不全以及政策文本更新导致的结论时效性问题。
defense_advice_zh: 将论文提出的四维量化指标纳入第三方供应商隐私尽调清单,作为合规问卷调查之外的量化补充。
在内部采用类似 LLM 抽取管线时,对抽取结果设置人工抽样复核机制,避免把模型误判直接用于合规结论。
关注分类法的覆盖范围与版本管理,记录数据元素与实践类型的定义变更,保证跨时间比较的可重复性。
对政策更新保持监测,定期重跑抽取与评分,防止基于历史快照的评分失效。
llm_summary.recommended_action_zh: 研究跟进

items.title: Design and Evaluation of a Controlled Post-Alert Incident Orchestration and Response Subsystem Using a Rule Engine and a Local Large Language Model
items.summary: This paper presents a controlled post-alert incident orchestration and response subsystem for educational information systems. The architecture separates deterministic classification, contextual analysis, human approval, and technical execution. A Rule Engine determines severity and selects the playbook, while Static RAG and a local large language model provide advisory content under Validator, Guardrail, Output Sanitizer, and Safe Fallback controls. Experiments begin after simulated alerts are stored in Elasticsearch. The Rule Engine matched the predefined routing matrix in all 30 boundary cases. The Durable Queue completed 100 events without duplicate tasks, new failed tasks, or unintended firewall rules. An eight-alert contention experiment preserved the configured limit of one active model request, and 30 sequential measurements showed an overall mean post-alert processing time of approximately 33 seconds. The results demonstrate functional correctness, traceability, controlled recovery, and bounded model integration within the evaluated laboratory scope.

llm_summary.summary_zh: 该论文提出并评估了一套面向教育信息系统的「告警后」受控事件编排与响应子系统（post-alert incident orchestration and response subsystem）。研究动机在于：传统自动化响应（SOAR 类）常把确定性判定、上下文分析与实际处置执行耦合在一起，一旦引入大语言模型，幻觉或越界输出可能直接触发危险动作，且难以审计与追溯。作者因此把流程显式拆成四个阶段：(1) 确定性分类——由规则引擎依据预定义的路由矩阵（routing matrix）判定告警严重级别并选择对应 playbook；(2) 上下文分析——采用 Static RAG（静态检索增强生成）配合本地部署的大语言模型，为处置提供建议性内容，而非直接执行；(3) 人工审批——由人决定是否采纳与下发；(4) 技术执行——由受控执行组件落实获批动作。为了约束模型行为，系统设置了四道防线：Validator（对模型输出做结构性校验）、Guardrail（策略护栏，限制允许的动作域）、Output Sanitizer（输出清洗，去除危险指令或多余内容）、Safe Fallback（安全回退，模型或校验环节异常时退回确定性路径）。实验设计上，模拟告警先写入 Elasticsearch，再进入该流水线。评估结果包括：规则引擎在全部 30 个边界用例上与预定义路由矩阵完全一致；持久化队列（Durable Queue）在 100 个事件的连续处理中没有产生重复任务、没有新增失败任务，也没有生成非预期的防火墙规则（即未出现越权或误配置执行）；一个八告警并发争用实验验证系统始终维持「同一时刻仅一个活跃模型请求」的配置上限；30 次顺序测量显示告警后处理的整体平均耗时约 33 秒。作者据此认为，在其实验室评估范围内，该设计达成了功能正确性、可追溯性、受控恢复以及有界（bounded）的模型集成。论文的局限也较明显：规模较小、环境为模拟实验室而非真实攻防环境，未涉及对抗性提示注入、模型被投毒或大规模真实告警负载等场景，端到端时延对生产级 SOC 而言也偏高。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 它给出了把 LLM 接入自动化响应的「有界集成」范式：确定性路由 + 人工审批 + 四层输出约束，并给出可复现的边界用例与并发上限验证方法，对正在把 LLM 塞进 SOAR/告警处置链路的团队有直接参考价值。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 可迁移到 SOAR/编排平台、教育或中小企业 SOC、以及任何「LLM 生成建议 + 自动化执行」的组合场景，尤其适用于需要在合规与审计要求下限制模型执行权限的环境。
detection_signals_zh: 同一时刻并发的模型推理请求数超过既定上限（配置为 1），可能意味着绕过了编排层或队列控制
出现未经人工审批即下发的防火墙/封禁类变更记录，或配置变更缺少对应的审批与 playbook 关联
队列中出现重复任务、重复执行同一 event id，或指向同一告警的多次执行记录
执行链路中缺失 Validator/Guardrail/Output Sanitizer 的校验日志，说明护栏被旁路或未生效
告警后处理时延显著偏离基线（实验室基线约 33 秒），可能提示模型回退到 Safe Fallback 或队列积压
同一告警的严重级别判定与预定义路由矩阵不一致，可能说明规则被篡改或配置漂移
defense_advice_zh: 对齐其分层思路：把确定性分级、模型建议、人工审批、实际执行解耦为独立组件，避免模型输出直连执行面
在模型输出与执行之间保留结构校验、策略护栏、输出清洗与安全回退四层控制，并确保回退路径在模型不可用时仍能走确定性流程
对模型请求做并发与速率硬限流，并把「同时活跃模型请求数」作为可观测指标持续监控
将每次处置的告警 ID、playbook、审批人、执行动作与校验结果写入不可篡改审计日志，保证可追溯
在真实环境上线前，用边界用例集与并发争用场景做验收，验证无重复任务、无失败任务、无非预期配置变更
明确实验室评估的局限：对外部 API 与 RAG 知识库投毒、提示注入等对抗场景另行做红队评估
llm_summary.recommended_action_zh: 研究跟进，并将「有界 LLM 集成 + 四层输出控制」模式纳入内部 SOAR/自动化响应架构评估的候选方案
